text:
maria: Quick question — when a route serves multiple model variants should per-route saved presets be owned at the route or model level? Seeing edge cases with quotas + rollouts.

jia: Are we talking about the Console saved filters / presets in the Route view?
maria: Yup. Example: /translate route uses model-english-v1 and model-english-v2 via rollout policy. If a PM saves a preset that pins quantized v1, do we show that preset to other teams that only have v2 access?
matt_p: Short answer: ownership needs two dimensions: visibility and enforcement. Visibility = who can see/apply a preset. Enforcement = whether applying a preset will be allowed given routing/quota constraints.
sara-eng: +1. Practically we also need to show when a preset is stale due to model deprecation or changed routing policies. UX should avoid silent failures.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: presets carry metadata: {owner, allowed_models, pinned_model_version, visibility} — and Console shows a badge if the pinned model is not available for current viewer.
lee: How does this interact with dedicated vs hosted? Dedicated customers can pin private models that hosted users don't see. Visibility rules must respect tenant boundaries.
ops-bot: Reminder: policy says cross-tenant visibility is forbidden. Any preset with dedicated-only model must be private to that tenant.
devex-bot: Also consider quota gating. If a preset requests a config that exceeds the viewer's quota (e.g., high token limit + low reserved capacity), show a warning and a disabled Apply button.
jia: UX sketch: add an 'applicability' pill next to saved presets: 
- green "applies" 
- yellow "applies with quota warnings" 
- red "blocked by routing/policy"
Include hover tooltip explaining why.
matt_p: For API folks: we need server-side check endpoints: `POST /ui/presets/apply-check` that returns {allowed: bool, reasons: [string], suggested_alternatives: [preset-id]}. Minimal payload: route_id, user_id, preset_id, current_context.
sara-eng: Can we reuse existing routing policy service? We already have /routing/evaluate which returns fallback chains. Might be better to enrich that response instead of creating a new endpoint.
matt_p: I looked — /routing/evaluate is synchronous and optimised for latency at request path; Console checks can be a bit heavier but should still reuse the core policy engine. Suggest add a lightweight wrapper that composes policy + quota checks.
maria: Backend privacy note: saved preset objects should not leak model variant ids to viewers lacking access. For those users, show an obfuscated description and a CTA to request access.
lee: Agree. For rollout UX, if a route is 10% -> v2, then applying a preset that pins v1 should show expected impact (e.g., "this preset will route 90% of traffic to v1 under current policy"). Maybe show a small bar chart.
jia: Good idea. Also record an event when a user applies a preset that overrides routing so we can monitor regressions.
sara-eng: Ops request — add an audit log entry: preset_apply:{user,preset,route,prev_policy,applied_at}. Helps debug when things break post-rollout.
matt_p: Implementation plan: 1) API: add apply-check endpoint that calls policy + quota + auth; 2) DB: augment preset schema with allowed_models list and visibility scopes; 3) Console: add pill + tooltips + small impact preview; 4) Telemetry: emit preset_apply and preset_check events.
maria: Timelines? We should aim to ship the Console UX + telemetry first as a feature flag (dev rollout) so Design and PMs can validate. Backend follow-up can iteratively tighten enforcement.
lee: I'll file a short RFC and include sample API contract + schema. tagging @matt_p @jia for review.
ops-bot: New RFC created: https://go/repo/rfcs/878-presets-ownership (private)
maria: Thanks — let's sync in the weekly Console sync. :thumbsup:
